response: There appears to be an association between elevated homocysteine levels and the development of vitiligo, a common skin disorder characterized by the loss of pigment-producing cells (melanocytes). In individuals who are predisposed to vitiligo, elevated homocysteine levels have been found to increase the risk of developing this condition. The biological role of vitamin B12 and folic acid in Hcy metabolism suggests that there may be a link between these nutrients and the development of vitiligo.
